target_customer: Publishers and developers who need to convert video into web and mobile formats via API
problem: Encoding video at scale required buying and running hardware and software; Zencoder offered it as a cloud API priced by minutes of video.
business_model: Usage-based API billed per minute of video encoded

founders.name: Jon Dahl
founders.background_notes: YC page says he co-founded Zencoder until its acquisition and later co-founded Mux (YC W16). Education not stated.

founders.name: Steve Heffernan
founders.role: Head of Product Design and Marketing
founders.background_notes: YC page credits him as creator of the Video.js player. Education not stated.

founders.name: Brandon Arbini
founders.role: VP of Product Development and Engineering
founders.background_notes: YC page lists only his title.

competitors.name: Encoding.com
competitors.what: Cloud video encoding SaaS billed per gigabyte

competitors.name: Flix Cloud (On2)
competitors.what: Encoding service built on the Zencoder team's own technology, shut down after Google bought On2

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable, fast, multi-format encoding at scale on elastic cloud infrastructure with a clean API; the team had prior experience from Flix Cloud.

defensibility.rationale: API integrations create some switching cost, but per minute encoding was a commodity and Amazon later launched a similar service.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Brightcove bought Zencoder in August 2012. Amazon launched Elastic Transcoder with a similar API and pricing less than a year later, according to a Mux blog post.

market_need_then: In 2010 web video was moving between Flash and HTML5 and many formats and devices needed support, and the closure of Flix Cloud sent customers looking for an alternative. Encoding.com's 2008 launch and 2010 raise show existing demand.

branding.domain_note: Used zencoder.com; it now redirects to a Brightcove product page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Developer focused: claimed integration in an afternoon with a well documented API (vendor claim).

branding.brand_signature: Video.js, the open source player created at Zencoder, carried a 2010 Zencoder copyright and built developer goodwill.

rebrands.why: Acquisition; Brightcove kept the Zencoder brand as a product.

branding.community_and_virality: Video.js adoption by developers; case studies such as Funny or Die used Zencoder and Video.js.

brand_strength.rationale: Known among developers and tied to Video.js, but a niche infrastructure brand with no consumer presence.

outcome_analysis: Zencoder spun out of the team that built Flix Cloud, joined YC in early 2010, launched in May 2010 with per minute API pricing, and benefited when Google shuttered Flix Cloud. It raised a $2 million round in April 2011 and was sold to Brightcove in August 2012 for about $27.4 million in the SEC filing, while press reported $30 million. Amazon's similar Elastic Transcoder arrived soon after, which shows the commodity risk the sale avoided.
notes: The 2010 seed amount was not found; a single aggregator listed a $100K seed and is unverified. The seed investors listed (YC, Dave McClure, Chris Sacca) come from search snippets of the company's own announcement text, so treat as partial. Brightcove filing price was about $27.4 million plus about $2.7 million retention payments; press said $30 million. Founder education and prior employers not found in opened sources. The Brightcove blog post on the raise could not be fetched.
